question: How long does childbirth take?

sources.title: Duration of spontaneous labour in ‘low-risk’ women with ‘normal’ perinatal outcomes: A systematic review - PMC

text: Childbirth can take very different lengths of time. NICE says the established first stage starts at 4 cm; on average it lasts about 8 hours in a first labour and 5 hours in a second or later labour, and is usually not over 18 or 12 hours. [1] A review found the active first stage and second stage vary a lot, with second stage often about 14–66 minutes in first births and 6–12 minutes in later births. [2]

text: You’re right — I should have said it more clearly. Childbirth can take hours to more than a day, and it depends on which stage you mean. WHO says the active first stage usually does not go beyond 12 hours in a first labour and 10 hours in later labours, and the second stage is usually within 3 hours and 2 hours. Lamaze says early labour can take about two-thirds of total labour time. [1][2]

sources.title: Factors affecting labor duration in Chinese pregnant women - PMC
Duration of spontaneous labour in ‘low-risk’ women with ‘normal’ perinatal outcomes: A systematic review - PMC

text: Usually it’s shorter the second time. NICE says the active first stage is shorter in later births, and the second stage is from full dilation to birth [1]. In one review, total labour in multiparous women was about 5.4–10.6 hours, with the second stage about 18–46 minutes [2]. Another review found the second stage in parous women varied widely, from a median 6–12 minutes to a 95th percentile of 58–76 minutes [3].
